We need to count carbonyl groups in the molecule. But we have no description of the molecule. Possibly the system expects us to retrieve NMR or IR to infer carbonyls. The simplest is to get IR spectra which shows C=O stretch. But counting carbonyl groups from IR may be ambiguous. Could also get carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-220 ppm). But we need the molecule; maybe the sample is preloaded as "the compound at hand". So we can just request IR spectra and look for C=O peaks. That would give number of carbonyls? IR may show multiple peaks. Could also get carbon NMR and count signals in carbonyl region.

We should minimize cost: maybe carbon NMR is cheaper? Not sure. Both are single calls. Let's get carbon NMR first, then count signals in carbonyl region (around 190-220 ppm). Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool.
